preregistration.question: How robustly can ACERO recover a KNOWN transit signal (Kepler-8b) against noise, gaps, detrending choices, cadence, multiple testing and instrumental artifacts, and under what conditions must it abstain? This is NOT a search for a new planet.

hypotheses.H0: noise + stellar trend only (no transit-like periodic dip)
hypotheses.H1: a periodic signal that is not transit-like (e.g. sinusoidal variability)
hypotheses.H2: the known transit of Kepler-8b (P~3.5225 d)
hypotheses.H3: an instrumental artifact (quarter boundary / roll / safe-mode gap)
hypotheses.H5: a flexible model that overfits detrending residuals
hypotheses.H6: data insufficient to distinguish the above

methods.note: Two pipelines over the SAME data are NOT independent replication.

detrending.rule: detrending windows/orders are fixed here; results are reported for ALL declared choices, never cherry-picked post hoc.

null_tests: control_star (real other star, no known transit)
phase_randomized (DECLARED: preserves power spectrum; only a null for transit SHAPE, not for periodicity — not used to test periodicity)

splits.train_test: odd/even quarters where possible; injection uses held-out noise realizations

allowed_claims: A transit-like periodic signal consistent with the known Kepler-8b ephemeris is recoverable in this public data under the declared methods.
Injected signals of stated SNR are recovered at the measured rate.
prohibited_claims: An injected signal is a real astrophysical observation.
Two pipelines over the same data constitute independent replication.
A single run confirms a belief in the World Model.

note: Hashed before any pipeline ran. Changing the plan changes this hash.
